cards.explanation: The answer is love. Paul, the apostle, says to be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. Everything else gets paid off, but this one stays open between believers. I think that's the only bill you'd ever want to see show up again next month.
The answer is True. Paul says it plainly: "For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law." Not part of the law, not the easy half. The law. I'd sign up for a deal like that all day long.

The answer is "Love your neighbor as yourself." Paul says the commandments, and any other commandments, are summed up in one decree, and the decree is "Love your neighbor as yourself." (Romans 13:9) That's a whole list squeezed into one sentence. I can't even fit my grocery list on one sticky note, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says it straight: "Love does no wrong to its neighbor." Then he adds, "Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law." Love isn't out there looking for ways to hurt anybody. Meanwhile my mustache knocks over a cookie box every other week.

The answer is slumber. Paul says, "The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber…" Notice he says the hour has come. It's not 'whenever you get around to it.' I've been through the sleeping part, friends, and waking up is better.

The answer is their salvation. Paul says, "…our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed." Every day gets them closer. That's the reason to be wide awake, and it's good news, not a scary one.

The answer is light. Paul says, "…let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light." Notice he says "us," so he's in this with them. You take off the dark stuff and you suit up in the light.

The answer is True. Paul says to behave decently, "…not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy." So dissension and jealousy sit right on the same list. They're named right alongside the rest, friends.

The answer is the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul says, "Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ…" He puts it right after the list of things to leave behind. Not the prophets, not the angels, but the Lord Jesus Christ Himself, friends.

The answer is False. There's no 'just in case' in this verse. Paul says, "…clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh." It's all in with Jesus, with no room set aside for the other stuff. And that's the last word of the passage.
